components.name: HCaptcha
components.usage: Bot protection for sign-up, login, password reset, and public contact forms. Renders hCaptcha's widget themed to the design system and writes the token into a hidden field so a plain form submit carries it; verify that token server-side before trusting the submission.

examples.label: Contact form with a visible challenge
examples.code:
<form method="post" action="/api/public/contact">
  <wa-input name="email" label="Email" type="email" required></wa-input>
  <HCaptcha siteKey={import.meta.env.VITE_HCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY} />
  <wa-button type="submit" variant="brand">Send</wa-button>
</form>

examples.label: Invisible challenge run from your own button

antipatterns: Trusting the token client-side, or gating a submit purely on onVerify without a server check.
Putting the hCaptcha secret key in client code or in the siteKey prop.
Adding hCaptcha's api.js with a <script> tag or hand-rolling the widget instead of using this component.
Using size="invisible" without calling execute() — no challenge ever runs.

components.name: ThemeEditor
components.usage: Drop in a panel that retunes the system's semantic colors, font stacks, type scale, spacing/density, corner radius, and shadow strength live. Overrides are applied as --wa-* custom properties on <html> and remembered in localStorage; serializeThemeCss() turns them into the CSS that belongs in src/webawesome/brand.css.

examples.label: Save into the brand file
Read overrides elsewhere
examples.code:
const { overrides, patch } = useThemeOverrides();
patch({ colors: { brand: "#7a2ff2" } });

antipatterns: Shipping theme changes only in localStorage — save them into brand.css so they reach every consumer.
Writing brand token overrides by hand in another stylesheet instead of brand.css.
Exposing the editor on a public production page: it is an authoring tool, and saving is refused outside development.
